claim.summary: One ASP State Home owns one hardened global server identity with authenticated, peer-UID-bound, replay-resistant socket admission.
claim.why: Identity drift, hint readiness, replay, insecure paths, unbounded resources, secret leakage, or cross-project dispatch would invalidate the runtime boundary.

illegalBranches.reason: Workspace and project identifiers cannot allocate a server identity.
The stopped state requires drain and checkpoint evidence.
Provider failure is isolated from the global server lifecycle.
Hint and socket-file presence are not authenticated liveness evidence.
Protocol or identity mismatch fails closed without endpoint mutation.
Kernel peer UID equality is necessary for secure admission.
Replay and nonce-capacity exhaustion fail closed without ledger mutation or eviction.
Runtime directories require current UID, non-symlink status, and 0700/0600 private modes.
Frame, connection, hook-worker, and drain overrun are rejected.
Sensitive log fields render only a redaction marker.

legalBranches.reason: The State Home is the complete modeled server identity.
projectId selects only the internal queue and provider partition.
Restart reaches ready only under explicit drain, checkpoint, and startup assumptions.
Connected, authenticated, protocol-matching, identity-matching handshake admits liveness.
Transport absence or refusal permits election unless operator stop has precedence.
Secure admission binds kernel peer UID and fresh nonce to the owner epoch.
Private path modes and explicit resource ceilings guard the socket boundary.
Security receipts disclose status without rendering secret field values.
